claim: Bernkastel's Marktplatz is the medieval heart of the old town, surrounded by an ensemble of half-timbered houses, today a lively meeting point with cafés, wine taverns and shops.
quote: The historic Marktplatz is the center of the medieval old town of Bernkastel-Kues, surrounded by an ensemble of half-timbered houses. Today the square is a lively meeting point with many cafés, wine taverns, and shops.

claim: The Spitzhäuschen on Bernkastel's market square is a slanted half-timbered house from 1416 built upward because taxes were calculated on ground area; it now houses a small wine tavern.
quote: The Spitzhäuschen is a slanted half-timbered house from 1416. It stands directly at the corner to Karlsstraße and seems to hover over the ground floor – this is because taxes were formerly calculated based on ground area, so people built upwards.

claim: Parking in Bernkastel-Kues is chargeable from 21 March to 31 December, daily 8am–7pm; large car parks sit by the bridge linking Bernkastel and Kues, with a 5–7 minute walk to the Marktplatz.
quote: Parking is chargeable from March 21 to December 31, daily from 8 am to 7 pm. Cell phone parking is available in the parking lots in Bernkastel-Kues.

claim: Landshut Castle rises 235m above Bernkastel on the castle hill, built late 13th century on Roman foundations by a Trier archbishop and destroyed by fire in 1692; reachable by car with free parking and a 5-minute walk.
quote: The ruins of Landshut Castle tower over the old town on the 235 m high castle hill. The castle was built at the end of the 13th century on the foundations of a Roman fortification by a Trier archbishop. In 1692 it was destroyed by an unfortunate fire

claim: The Cusanusstift / St. Nikolaus-Hospital in Kues was founded 3 December 1458 by Nikolaus von Kues as an almshouse for 33 men and holds a world-famous library and wine museum, about 450 m from the Marktplatz.
quote: Nikolaus von Kues founded the facility on December 3, 1458 as a poor hospital for exactly 33 single men from nobility, clergy, and citizens.

claim: The Wittlich Tourist-Information sits in the Old Town Hall (a listed building on the historic market square) at Marktplatz/Neustraße 2; guided city walks and museum visits are bookable on request.
quote: The tourist information office is located in the Old Town Hall, a listed building on the historic market square. Guided city walks and museum visits can be booked on request.

claim: Wittlich's market square is an art-historical gem of 18th- and early-19th-century patrician houses anchored by the Renaissance Old Town Hall rebuilt after the 1647 fire; the Türmchen is a 1317 fortification remnant.
quote: The market square is an art-historical gem with beautiful patrician and bourgeois houses from the 18th and early 19th centuries, featuring the Old Town Hall, an imposing Renaissance building erected after the city fire of 1647.

claim: Manderscheid has two medieval castle ruins facing each other across the Lieser river just above the town; the Oberburg is open year-round with free admission and the Niederburg can be visited by guided tour or self-guided.
quote: The Upper Castle is open year-round and has free admission. The lower castle can be explored on guided tours - even at night - or on your own; it only remains closed in bad weather.

claim: Manderscheid's Niederburg is open daily 11:00–17:00 from April through November, and weekends only 12:00–15:00 from December through March.
quote: April – November: Daily 11:00 – 17:00 Uhr ... Dezember – März: Only Saturday and Sunday 12:00 – 15:00 Uhr

claim: Traben-Trarbach's signature sights include the Art-Nouveau Brückentor by Bruno Möhring, the Grevenburg castle ruin and the Mont Royal fortress built for Louis XIV in 1687 by Vauban high above Traben.
quote: Historical sites like the Brückentor, the castle ruin Grevenburg and the fortress Mont Royal are typical for Traben-Trarbach.

claim: Traben-Trarbach was the second-largest wine-trading town in Europe after Bordeaux around 1900, leaving vast wine cellars beneath the town that can be visited as the 'Traben-Trarbach Underworld' on guided tours.
quote: The Art Nouveau town on the Mosel was, around 1900, the second largest wine transshipment point in Europe, right after the large French city of Bordeaux.

claim: Daun sits in the volcanic Eifel beside the three Daun Maars (Gemündener, Weinfelder, Schalkenmehrener) and offers spa gardens, the Dunaris healing spring and a centre with shops; the Eifelsteig and Lieserpfad pass through to Manderscheid.
quote: Daun is a small town nestled in the rolling hills of the volcanic Eifel and in the immediate vicinity of the three most famous volcanic lakes in the Eifel, the Daun Maars.

claim: The Dronke Tower / Mäuseberg loop above the Weinfelder Maar from Daun is a 5.3 km easy walk taking about 1h32; a longer loop circles all three Daun Maars.
quote: The most popular easy hiking route is Dronke Tower on the Mäuseberg – View of the Weinfelder Maar loop from Daun, a 3.3 miles (5.3 km) trail that takes 1 hour 32 minutes to complete.

claim: Bernkastel-Kues and Traben-Trarbach are just 5.75 km apart as the crow flies, and Traben-Trarbach is 16.55 km from Wittlich.
quote: Traben-Trarbach to Wittlich: 16.55 km (air line) ... Bernkastel-Kues to Traben-Trarbach: 5.75 km (air line)

claim: Wittlich to Bernkastel-Kues is about 11 miles (≈17 km) by road, roughly a 16-minute drive.
quote: The driving distance between Wittlich and Bernkastel-Kues is 11 miles, and it takes approximately 16 minutes to drive.

claim: Manderscheid lies 11.81 km from Daun in a straight line, well within a half-day combined visit from Dreis.
quote: The shortest distance between Manderscheid and Daun is 11.81 km in a straight line.

claim: Bernkastel-Kues' Christmas market runs 20 Nov 2026–2 Jan 2027 at weekends and special days, with stalls of decorations, wine and crafts among the half-timbered facades.
quote: international and national exhibitors will be presenting high-quality decorations, gift ideas, culinary specialties, wine products, antiques and creative fashion and jewelry designs in a Christmassy atmosphere from 20.11.2026-02.01.2027

claim: Wittlich's Säubrennerkirmes, one of Rhineland-Palatinate's largest fairs (~100,000 visitors), takes over the market square and surrounding streets on the third weekend of August.
quote: The Säubrennerkirmes has developed into one of the largest festivals in Rhineland-Palatinate with approximately one hundred thousand visitors per year since its first occurrence in 1950.

claim: Burg Landshut above Bernkastel-Kues is a 13th-century summer residence of the Archbishops of Trier built on a late-Roman 'Princastellum' fort, with a 30 m keep, barrier-free circular path, on-site restaurant and panoramic Mosel views; reachable on foot in ~30 min from the market square, by car, or by the yellow Burg Landshut Express.
quote: unusually massive remains of a Roman fortification (fort)... dominates the hilltop above Bernkastel with its impressive 30-meter-high keep and fortress walls... barrier-free circular route around the grounds

claim: Burg Landshut was destroyed by fire in 1692, sits about a half-hour walk from Bernkastel-Kues old town, and entry to the castle grounds is free with only a small fee to climb the tower.
quote: built in the 13th century as a summer residence for the Archbishops of Trier, and it was destroyed by fire in 1692... Entry to the castle grounds is free, with only a small fee to climb the tower.

claim: The Oberburg Manderscheid, first recorded 1141-1146 and destroyed by French troops in 1673, is a freely accessible ruin with a five-storey bergfried visitors can climb for views over the Niederburg and the Lieser valley.
quote: Ruins with a five-story fighting tower (bergfried) that visitors can access... destroyed by French troops in 1673... thoroughly renovated in 1921 by the municipality of Manderscheid

claim: Grevenburg above Traben-Trarbach was built in 1350 by Count Johann III of Sponheim-Starkenburg, changed hands 13 times during 17th-18th century wars, and was finally destroyed by the French in 1734 — today an ~700 m² ruin reached by a ~30-min climb from Trarbach with a castle tavern in season.
quote: The castle was built in 1350 by the Count Johann III of Sponheim-Starkenburg... the castle changed hands 13 times... destroyed by the French in 1734... extending over an area of around 700 square metres.

claim: Grevenburg ruins are freely accessible year-round and feature a seasonal castle tavern and garden with sweeping views over the Mosel loop.
quote: Today, visitors can explore the castle ruins, which feature a cozy tavern and castle garden integrated into the remaining structures. The location offers scenic vistas overlooking the Mosel River valley.

claim: Burg Arras near Alf was a Roman border station and imperial castle; today the Keuthen family runs it as a 10-room castle hotel, restaurant and museum, with day visits Saturday-Monday from 11:00 (reservation required), museum admission €6, featuring the original castle dungeon and tower visit.
quote: the only castle hotel on the Mosel... admission priced at €6.00... Saturday, Sunday, Monday from 11:00 AM (reservation required)

claim: Burg Arras was destroyed by French troops during the War of the Austrian Succession and rebuilt over a century ago as a noble residence; the on-site museum is dedicated to former German President Dr. Heinrich Lübke and showcases local cultural treasures, the original dungeon and a tower visit.
quote: destroyed by the French during the War of the Austrian Succession, and was rebuilt more than 100 years ago as a noble residence... castle museum is dedicated to former German President Dr. Heinrich Lübke

claim: Marienburg above Pünderich/Zell perches on a peninsula inside the 14 km Mosel loop with three superimposed architectural layers (12th-century manor, late-Gothic 15th-c. choir, 18th-c. raised choir) and today operates as a youth education centre — visitable only from the outside.
quote: the manor house dates back to the 12th century, the late Gothic choir from the second half of the 15th century, and the elevated choir masonry with oval windows from the 18th century... Marienburg is a youth education center and can only be visited from the outside.

claim: The Prinzenkopfturm, a ~10-minute walk from Marienburg, is freely accessible day and night and is considered one of the most beautiful viewpoints on the Mosel, looking down on the Pünderich hillside viaduct and the Zeller Hamm bend.
quote: the Prinzenkopf observation tower, approximately 10 minutes' walk from Marienburg Castle, is considered one of the most beautiful vantage points on the Moselle. The Prinzenkopf Tower is open at all times.

claim: Schloss Lieser, designed by Heinrich Theodor Schmidt in 1884-1887 for industrialist Eduard Puricelli and enlarged for his son-in-law Clemens von Schorlemer in 1904-1906, combines a Neo-Renaissance block with a later Art Nouveau wing inspired by Palladian villas; Kaiser Wilhelm II stayed here in 1906, 1911 and 1913, and today it houses a 49-room Marriott Autograph Collection hotel.
quote: designed by architect Heinrich Theodor Schmidt in 1884–1887 as the residence for the family of winery owner Eduard Puricelli... Kaiser Wilhelm II stayed in 1906, 1911 and 1913.

claim: Schloss Lieser sits directly on the Mosel riverbank in the village of Lieser (~15 km from Dreis) and is open as a luxury hotel with restaurant, spa, indoor pool and library accessible to non-resident diners.
quote: Nestled in the heart of the Moselle Valley, directly on the riverbank and surrounded by vineyards... 49 luxurious and individually appointed guest rooms and suites.

claim: Burg Eltz, the famously intact fairy-tale Mosel castle, sits ~62 km / 1 h 3 min by car from Wittlich and therefore falls outside the 30 km radius from Dreis — it is a feasible half-day outing but not a 'local' detour.
quote: The distance between Wittlich to Burg Eltz is 36 miles, with a road distance of 38.3 miles (approximately 62 km). The fastest way to get from Wittlich to Burg Eltz is to drive which takes 1 hour 3 minutes.

claim: Markus Molitor's Klosterberg vinothek in Zeltingen-Rachtig is open daily 10:00-17:00.
quote: Our vinotheque is open daily from 10:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

claim: Markus Molitor offers tastings of more than 40 wines at Haus Klosterberg in Bernkastel-Wehlen, by reservation.
quote: In the special atmosphere of the vinotheque at Klosterberg House... you can enjoy unique wine tastings, choosing your personal selection from more than 40 different wines.

claim: Weingut Dr. Loosen at St. Johannishof in Bernkastel-Kues is family-owned for over 200 years and led by Ernst Loosen, specialising in great Rieslings.
quote: Family-owned for over 200 years, the winery combines a rich tradition with a clear vision for the highest quality.

claim: Dr. Loosen tastings (1-40 people, German/English) are by appointment Mon-Sat 10:00-17:00 in high season; closed Sundays.
quote: We are in the high season for wine tastings and wine purchases from Monday to Saturday between 10 AM and 5 PM by appointment. On Sundays and public holidays, the wine shop is closed.

claim: Weingut Schloss Lieser, led by Thomas Haag (Winzer des Jahres 2015), works eight VDP.Grosse Lage sites including Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr, Wehlener Sonnenuhr and Bernkasteler Doctor.
quote: Thomas Haag won the title Winzer des Jahres (Winemaker of the Year) in 2015 and achieved the fifth grape, the highest category in both the Gault Millau and Eichelmann wine guides.

claim: Schloss Lieser is a VDP member estate in the Mosel region.
quote: VDP.Weingut Schloss Lieser

claim: J.J. Prüm in Wehlen, founded 1911 and now led by Dr Katharina Prüm, farms 13.5 ha of vines exclusively planted to Riesling on slate slopes.
quote: The estate is run by Dr Katharina Prüm who watches over 13.5 hectares of vines... Only Riesling is grown and harvested there.

claim: Joh. Jos. Prüm is a VDP estate; visits and tastings are by advance appointment.
quote: VDP.Estate J. J. Prüm

claim: Weingut Fritz Haag in Brauneberg farms 19.5 ha including 8 ha in the Grosse Lage Juffer and Juffer Sonnenuhr sites with slopes to 80%.
quote: The vineyards cover 19.5 hectares of vines with slopes of up to 80%, eight hectares of which are in the top Brauneberg sites of Juffer and Juffer Sonnenuhr.

claim: The Juffer-Sonnenuhr is the steepest, most south-facing portion of the Brauneberg hillside and produces Fritz Haag's flagship Grosse Lage wines.
quote: The Juffer-Sonnenuhr vineyard is the steepest and most south-facing part of the Brauneberg hillside, surrounded by the Juffer vineyard, and this Grosse Lage (Grand Cru) site produces profound, distinctive wines with great purity and concentration.

claim: Selbach-Oster in Zeltingen-Rachtig (Gänsfelder Straße 20) offers Riesling tastings by request, except during harvest until end of October.
quote: Wine tastings are gladly possible upon request. Wine tastings are not available during the harvest (until about the end of October).

claim: Moselsteig Stage 10 (Kesten/Osann-Monzel to Bernkastel-Kues) crosses the Brauneberger Juffer vineyard with views from Monzeler Kätzchen and ends at Landshut Castle above Bernkastel.
quote: The trail passes impressive rocky cliffs with splendid visible layers of slate and crosses world-renowned vineyards, such as Braunberger Juffer.

claim: Moselsteig Stage 11 continues from Bernkastel-Kues through the Wehlener Sonnenuhr and Ürziger Würzgarten vineyards toward Ürzig.
quote: Moselsteig Trail Stage 11: Bernkastel-Kues – Ürzig

claim: The Wine Festival of the Middle Mosel runs 3-7 September 2026 in Bernkastel-Kues with a wine route, Saturday fireworks and Sunday parade.
quote: Wine festival of the Middle Mosel in Bernkastel-Kues 03.09.2026

claim: The Middle Moselle Wine Festival features a 300-metre wine route with 20+ vendors and adds guided wine hikes new for 2026.
quote: Wine Route - a 300-meter stretch with over 20 wine vendors offering 'Riesling and other types of wine'... Special wine hiking tours (new for 2026)

claim: The Brauneberg Wine Festival runs 4-7 June 2026 at Moselweinstraße 101 with three local wineries (Fehres, Heil, Boujong) and live music.
quote: Dates: June 4-7, 2026, starting at 11:00 AM each day... Three renowned wineries participate—Harald Konrad Fehres, Rainer Heil, and Boujong

claim: Mythos Mosel 2026 (29-31 May) brings 116 winegrowers to 29 stations between Kesten and Zeltingen-Rachtig with shuttle buses from Mülheim; tickets €60 Saturday, €30 Sunday.
quote: Overall, 116 winegrowers will present their wines at 29 stations between Kesten and Zeltingen-Rachtig... Tickets are only available in advance, €60 on Saturday and €30 on Sunday.

claim: The Brauneberger Juffer slope reaches 80% gradient and has been a top site since Roman times, with Napoleon pricing its wines above all other Mosel wines.
quote: The riverbank opposite Brauneberg is a steep, south-facing slope that reaches a gradient of 80 percent... Napoleon paid tribute to the Brauneberger wines by fixing their prices above those of all other Mosel wines.

claim: The Maare-Mosel-Radweg runs ~58 km from Daun to Bernkastel-Kues, mostly on a former railway line, asphalted with gentle gradients, featuring viaducts, tunnels and Eifel maar viewpoints.
quote: The route runs entirely on the former railway line from Daun to Lieser... continuously asphalted path has hardly any inclines but plenty of opportunities to rest and sights: two viaducts, numerous bridges, four tunnels, as well as Eifel maars and extinct volcanoes.

claim: A circular hike around all three Dauner Maare from Schalkenmehren is ~9.5 km (5.9 mi), moderate, ~1,145 ft elevation gain, takes 3–3.5 hours.
quote: A moderate hike covers 5.9 mi, with an elevation gain of 1,145 ft, taking about 3–3.5 hr to complete... begins at the Schalkenmehren bus stop and then leads in several laps around the three unique volcanic lakes.

claim: The 11-metre Dronketurm stands on the 561 m Mäuseberg between Weinfelder and Schalkenmehrener Maar; 43 steps lead to panoramic views over the three Dauner Maare and on clear days as far as the Hunsrück and Nürburg.
quote: the eleven-meter-high tower... 43 steps... a wonderful view awaits you of the Gemünden Maar... on the plateau on the 561-metre-high Mäuseberg

claim: The Lieserpfad runs ~74 km in four daily stages of 15–21 km, from the Lieser source near Boxberg to the Mosel at Lieser; took 2nd place in Germany's most beautiful hiking trail vote in 2018.
quote: The 74 km long Lieser Trail can be easily completed in four daily stages between 15 and 21 km in length... In 2018, the Lieserpfad achieved 2nd place as Germany's most beautiful hiking trail!

claim: Lieserpfad Stage 3 Manderscheid–Wittlich is ~23 km with ~760 m elevation gain, the trail's longest stage, passing the Manderscheid castles and steep Lieser valley.
quote: Lieserpfad: Stage 3: Manderscheid-Wittlich

claim: The Burgenklettersteig Manderscheid is the only via ferrata in Rhineland-Palatinate, ~4.6 km in three stages with difficulties A–D including a 60 m rope bridge; equipment (helmet, harness, set) can be rented at the GesundLand Tourist-Information Kurhaus.
quote: Burgenklettersteig Manderscheid Vulkaneifel

claim: The Manderscheider Burgenstieg with Rittersteig is a 5.4 km family-friendly loop through the Lieser valley with the Belvedere lookout offering classic views of both castle ruins (Niederburg, Oberburg).
quote: With a distance of 5.4 kilometres, it is also a popular hike for families. It runs around Manderscheid into the romantic Lieser valley and up to the Belvedere lookout point.

claim: Eifelsteig Stage 11 Daun–Manderscheid is ~20–23 km with ~700 m elevation gain (hard), passing all three Daun Maare before descending into the Lieser valley to Manderscheid.
quote: The trail covers 20.4 km with an elevation gain of 702 m and takes about 6.5–7 hours to complete... starts in Daun and first leads to the Daun maars.

claim: Dreis bei Wittlich sits 7 km northeast of Wittlich, ~29 km north of Daun and ~14 km southwest of Schweich, placing the Dauner Maare, Manderscheid and Bernkastel-Kues all inside the 30 km radius.
quote: Dreis bei Wittlich is 7 km northeast of Wittlich, 29 km north of Daun

claim: The VulkaMaar Trail (Vulkaneifel-Pfad) won 'Germany's Most Beautiful Hiking Trail' in 2021 and passes the Meerfelder Maar and the Windsborn Crater Lake (Germany's only above-ground crater lake) plus the Wolfsschlucht ravine.
quote: The VulkaMaar Trail was voted Germany's most beautiful hiking trail in 2021... passing by maars like the Meerfelder Maar and the Windsborn Crater Lake, and traversing areas like the Wolfsschlucht ravine.

claim: The HeimatSpur 'MaareGlück' premium short trail is 11 km and links all three water-filled Daun Maare plus the Schalkenmehrener fen and dry maar.
quote: The HeimatSpur MaareGlück trail covers 11 km and includes water-filled maars, a fen and a dry maar at Schalkenmehren.

claim: Villa Otrang outdoor area is freely accessible year-round; protective buildings with mosaics open April–October Wed–Sun 10:00–17:00; free admission.
quote: Außenanlage und zwei Schutzbauten mit Mosaiken sind von April bis Oktober von Mittwoch bis Sonntag, 10 bis 17 Uhr, geöffnet.

claim: Villa Otrang was a major Roman villa rustica with a manor house of over 60 rooms, baths, hypocaust heating and surviving mosaic floors.
quote: The manor house was magnificent in size with over 60 rooms. In addition to the impressive manor house, the complex included several baths, a heating system (hypocaust) and a temple area.

claim: Villa Otrang is located near Fließem about 5 km north of Bitburg; 14 of its 66 rooms once had mosaics, four of which survive nearly intact.
quote: Die Villa Otrang ist international bekannt für ihre prachtvollen Mosaikfußböden, mit denen 14 der 66 Räume des Herrenhauses ehemals ausgestattet waren, von denen vier bis heute fast unversehrt erhalten sind.

claim: The Roman double burial chamber at Nehren preserves original 4th-century wall and vault paintings in the left chamber – unique north of the Alps – viewable through a window in the door.
quote: The burial chamber of the first tomb is the only ancient room still existing in the Rhineland where the original paintings on the walls and vault are largely preserved.

claim: The Nehren Roman tombs are two reconstructed funerary temples; chamber I measures 2.6 m wide, 4.3 m deep, 3 m high with a barrel vault and best-preserved vault paintings north of the Alps.
quote: Die besser erhaltene Grabkammer I des linken Tempels ist 2,6 m breit, 4,3 m tief und 3 m hoch und besitzt ein Tonnengewölbe.

claim: Mittelmosel-Museum (Barockvilla Böcking, Traben-Trarbach) reopens 1 April 2026; Tue–Fri 10:00–17:00 and Sat–Sun 12:00–16:00; adults €5, family €10.
quote: From April 1, 2026, the museum is open Tuesday to Friday from 10:00 to 17:00, and Saturday to Sunday from 12:00 to 16:00.

claim: The Mittelmoselmuseum's 20+ rooms hold Roman and Frankish archaeology, Mont Royal fortress finds, 1,100 Delft tiles in the dining room, and the Spies collection of furniture and art.
quote: The museum houses an extensive collection on the history of Traben-Trarbach, including archaeological finds from Roman and Frankish periods. The dining room is decorated with 1,100 Delft tiles.

claim: The Cusanus-Geburtshaus museum in Bernkastel-Kues is closed December 2025 through February 2026, reopening in March 2026 for the season.
quote: Das Cusanus-Geburtshaus (Museum) ist in den Monaten Dezember 2025, Januar und Februar 2026 geschlossen!

claim: The St-Nikolaus-Hospital / Cusanusstift library in Bernkastel-Kues – holding 314 medieval manuscripts from Cusanus's bequest – is only viewable on guided tours April–October Tue 10:30 and Fri 15:00.
quote: The library contains 314 manuscripts from the 9th to 15th centuries... Visits are offered from April to October on Tuesdays at 10:30 AM and Fridays at 3:00 PM.

claim: Vulkanhaus Strohn summer hours from 1 April 2026 are Tue–Sun 10:00–17:00; admission €3 adult, €2 reduced, €6 family.
quote: From April 1, 2026 onwards, it's open Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00... Admission costs €3 for adults, €2 for reduced rates, and a family card (couple and children) is €6.

claim: Vulkanhaus Strohn is the central exhibition house of the Geopark Vulkaneifel, presenting the geology and volcanic history of the Eifel with the famous lava bomb outside.
quote: Das Vulkanhaus Strohn ist das zentrale Ausstellungshaus des Natur- und Geoparks Vulkaneifel.

claim: Kreismuseum Bitburg-Prüm covers regional history with Stone Age, Roman and Frankish finds; open March–October Tue–Wed 11–17, Thu–Fri & Sun 14–17 (closed Mon, Sat).
quote: March - October: Tuesdays and Wednesdays 11 AM - 5 PM, Thursdays, Fridays, and Sundays 2 PM - 5 PM (closed Mondays and Saturdays)

claim: Dreis (home of Waldhotel Sonnora) is in the Bernkastel-Wittlich district at the edge of the Wittlich Depression on the river Salm, belonging to the Verbandsgemeinde of Wittlich-Land.
quote: Dreis is an Ortsgemeinde – a municipality belonging to a Verbandsgemeinde... in the Bernkastel-Wittlich district in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. The municipality lies on the river Salm at the point where it flows out of the Eifel at the foot of the Burgberg, on the edge of the Wittlich Depression.

claim: Wild- und Erlebnispark Daun runs 15 Mar–14 Nov 10:00–18:00 (winter 10:00–16:00) with 2026 admission €18 adult, €16 child (4–15), family ticket €60, and offers an 8-km car safari, falconry, monkey canyon, adventure playground and summer toboggan run.
quote: Erwachsene: 18,00 € · Kinder (4-15 Jahre): 16,00 € · Familienpaket (2 Erw. + 2 Kinder): 60,00 €

claim: Wildpark Daun spans roughly 250 hectares of forest and meadow with native wildlife observable along a car safari, plus an adventure playground and summer toboggan (extra charge).
quote: approximately 250 hectares of forest and meadow terrain with numerous mostly native wildlife species... 8-kilometer car safari route and various attractions including a bird of prey enclosure, a barbary macaque gorge, an adventure playground, and a summer toboggan run

claim: Bitburger Erlebniswelt brewery tour in Bitburg runs ~1 hour with bookings required; €9 adults (16+), €5 ages 12–15, free under 12, including two drinks and a pretzel bar in the Bit-Lounge.
quote: Admission costs €9 for adults aged 16 and over. Children from 12 to 15 years pay €5.00. Children under 12 years have free admission. This includes the guided tour as well as two free drinks and a pretzel bar in the Bit Lounge.

claim: Cochemer Sesselbahn chairlift operates 28 Mar–15 Nov 2026 with 2026 fares of €5.90/€7.90 (adult single/return), €2.90/€3.90 (child 4–14), and a family card €20 return for up to 4 children.
quote: Children (4-14 years) €2.90 / €3.90 · Adults (14+) €5.90 / €7.90 · Family card (2-4 children) €20.00

claim: Cochem lies ~26.6 km as the crow flies from Wittlich, placing it at the outer edge of a 30-km radius from Dreis (which sits south of Wittlich).
quote: The shortest distance between Cochem and Wittlich is 26.57 km as the crow flies.

claim: The Naturfreibad Schalkenmehrener Maar (near Daun) opens 1 Jun–14 Sep 2026 from 10:00–19:00 with a baby pool, toddler pool, diving board and water slide; entry €5 adult, €3 child 4–17, free under 4.
quote: Adult admission is €5.00, children aged 4-17 cost €3.00, and children up to 3 years have free entry... open from June 1, 2026 to September 14, 2026, from 10:00–19:00.

claim: The Maarmuseum in Manderscheid uses interactive media to tell the volcanic maar story, with a 45-million-year-old Eckfeld primeval-horse skeleton, climbing-volcano playground and zip line; €3 adult / €2 child, combi ticket with Niederburg €3.50.
quote: Maarmuseum Manderscheid... The highlight is the 'Eckfelder Urpferdchen,' an almost completely preserved skeleton of a pregnant mare from 45 million years ago... features a playground with a climbing volcano and zip line. Admission is €3.00 for adults and €2.00 for children ages 4-17

claim: Manderscheid's twin castles — the Niederburg (paid, daily 11:00–17:00 Apr–Nov, €2 adult / €0.70 child) and the freely accessible Oberburg ruin — sit ~15 km from Dreis and add a low-cost, hands-on medieval stop to a Maarmuseum visit.
quote: The Niederburg can be visited daily from April to November between 11:00 and 17:00. The Oberburg can be visited free of charge daily. Admission to the Niederburg costs €2.00 for adults and €0.70 for children aged 5-15

claim: Eifelpark Gondorf (8 km east of Bitburg) opens for the 2026 main season on 28 March with day tickets €37.50 (≥150 cm), €34.50 (105–149 cm), free under 105 cm; afternoon 'Schnupperrunde' from 15:30 is €20.
quote: Visitors 150cm and taller: €37.50 · Visitors 105-149cm: €34.50 · Children under 105cm: Free · Schnupperrunde (afternoon entry after 3:30 PM): €20.00 · gültig ab 28.03.2026

claim: Eifelpark Gondorf combines a wildlife park with about 60 rides including a summer toboggan, rapids ride and roller-coaster, sitting roughly 8 km east of Bitburg.
quote: Der Eifelpark bietet 60 Attraktionen und viele Wildtiere, darunter eine Sommerrodelbahn, Wildwasserbahn und Achterbahn... Eifelpark ist 8 km östlich von Bitburg

claim: The Burg Landshut Express — a vintage yellow shuttle bus, not a chairlift — runs hourly daily Apr–Oct from Am Gestade in Bernkastel up to the Landshut castle ruin above the Mosel meander.
quote: The 'Burg-Landshut Express' runs daily from 11:00 - 17:00 on the hour (from April to October). It departs hourly from 10 to 18 Uhr from the stop 'Am Gestade'... bright yellow Burg Landshut Express brings you quickly and reliably to the gates of Landshut Castle

claim: Bowling Room Trier (Franz-Georg-Straße 125, Trier) bundles modern bowling lanes, laser tag and arcade with food and bar service, open Wed–Thu 17:00–22:00, Fri–Sat to 01:00 and Sun 11:00–21:00 — the nearest one-stop indoor entertainment center to Dreis since Wittlich itself lacks an equivalent.
quote: Bowlingroom Trier is the address for laser tag, arcade games and bowling in Trier... closed Monday and Tuesday, open 5:00 PM - 10:00 PM Wednesday and Thursday, 5:00 PM - 1:00 AM Friday and Saturday, and 11:00 AM - 9:00 PM Sunday

claim: Only eight ferries still cross the Mosel; within day-trip range from Dreis the Alf–Bullay 'Remigius' (passenger/bike, sub-5-minute crossing) is the most accessible novelty stop, while the car-and-passenger 'St. Josef' Ellenz-Poltersdorf–Beilstein cable ferry runs daily in season.
quote: Remigius (Alf–Bullay): Passenger and bicycle ferry... Small ferry taking under five minutes; cars must use the nearby bridge... St. Josef (Ellenz-Poltersdorf–Beilstein): Car and passenger ferry... Motor-assisted cable ferry operating daily during tourist season

claim: Vulkaneifel-Therme in Bad Bertrich (Germany's only Glauber's-salt thermal spring, 32 °C) is the closest true thermal spa to Dreis, but in 2026 the steam bath is under renovation from 8 Jun to early September and the full therme closes 15–28 Jun for maintenance.
quote: The Vulkaneifel Therme will be closed from June 15-28, 2026 for cleaning and maintenance work. Additionally, the steam bath will be renovated starting June 8, 2026 until early September 2026

claim: Eifel-Therme Zikkurat — often paired with Bitburg in listings — is actually in Mechernich (North Rhine-Westphalia), well over 60 km from Dreis and outside a 30-km radius despite its 'Eifel' branding.
